decision: closed_no_credit: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use.
summary: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. The only full-text source (40615851, 21 RCTs, 1705 knee-OA patients) shows lower CRP and TNF-alpha but no change in ESR, IL-1beta, IL-6 or PGE2, with mixed curcumin products, multi-herb formulas and active comparators; it does not measure OA pain or function. The two umbrella reviews (38576215, 38945354) are abstract-only, pool overlapping meta-analyses and report no preparation or dose. With Dr. Pham's rejection of preparation-wide approval for this generic turmeric/curcuminoid record, no source supports credit; reference-only removes Evidence points from its products.

identity.preparation: Curcumin-based medications (13 trials), multi-ingredient curcumin formulas (6: Acujoint, Instaflex, CartiJoint Forte, RA-11, NXT15906F6) and curcumin plus NSAID (2); not turmeric root powder

population.description: 21 RCTs, 1705 knee-osteoarthritis patients (852 intervention, 853 control), mean ages 48-71 years, seven countries.

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs; controls were placebo (11), NSAIDs (7), paracetamol (1) or glucosamine plus chondroitin (2).

outcomes.name: ESR, IL-1beta, IL-6 and PGE2: no significant difference versus control

limitations: Surrogate inflammatory biomarkers only; this source does not assess osteoarthritis pain or function, the record's Joint & Bone Health claim.

Mixed preparations including multi-herb formulas and curcumin-plus-NSAID arms, and active comparators; cannot isolate a turmeric/curcumin preparation. Dr. Pham's returned decision rejects broad preparation-wide approval.

Declared umbrella reviews 38576215 (11 meta-analyses, OA VAS/WOMAC improved) and 38945354 (21 meta-analyses, biomarkers) were inspected at abstract level only (no open full text); they report no regimens and pool overlapping meta-analyses, so they supply no verified dose, preparation or included-trial list and no credit-bearing context.
Curcumin 80-1500 mg/day for 1 week to 4 months; no root-to-extract or bioavailability conversion.
